sources.title: Overview | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Cloud agents are accessible through browser/desktop/mobile clients and shared multiplayer workspaces.

sources.title: Desktop apps | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: macOS 13+ Intel/ARM and Linux AppImage/deb clients; Windows coming soon; desktop push not yet available.

sources.title: Mobile apps | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Native iOS/iPad app supports tickets, chat, diffs and PRs. Android uses a PWA, with opt-in browser/mobile push.

sources.title: Agents | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Cursor, Pi, Muse Code, OpenCode, Amp and Factory Droid run in cloud environments.

sources.title: Agent credentials | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Subscriptions and API keys are separate routes. Connected-plan quota exhaustion stops work without automatic API fallback.

sources.title: Superconductor API | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: PAT API reads project tickets/chats/diffs, creates tickets with optional default-agent launch and sends messages; existing-ticket launch and PR creation are not available.

sources.title: Skills and MCPs | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Project-scoped MCP connectors, Playwright and repository skills are configured for agents.

sources.title: Connectors | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Personal/workspace connectors inherit external permissions and project sharing; custom MCP is supported.

sources.title: Superconductor skills | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Agents read project ticket/chat/diff records and create tickets with optional default-agent launch. They cannot change existing tickets or read saved artifacts.

sources.title: Quick start | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Connect repositories, provider credentials and a development environment before launching a ticket.

sources.title: Tickets | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Native tickets have states and multiple implementations, searchable dashboards, stars and local drafts; implementation picker launches up to twelve per action.

sources.title: Implementations | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Independent implementations receive separate branches/environments, explicit status, estimated costs and PR create/update actions.

sources.title: Chat | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Workspace collaborators share chat, presence and inputs. Claude supports mid-turn steering; others queue. Model changes apply to later turns within a harness.

sources.title: Diff & Guided Review | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Full/uncommitted diffs, anchored comments, Guided Review and changes-requested follow-ups are documented.

sources.title: QA Checks [Beta] | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Private-beta QA agent checks ticket requirements, code quality and tests; not a generally available gate.

sources.title: Artifacts | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Images, documents, recordings and files are saved with implementations and have viewers.

sources.title: Development environment | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Automatic setup configures packages/build/start commands and previews; snapshots and encrypted/redacted environment secrets are documented.

sources.title: Lifecycle | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Cloud environments retain files while idle-paused but not processes. Startup commands rerun; failed snapshot builds retain last successful snapshot.

sources.title: Network sandboxing | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Network allowlists have provider/platform exceptions. Users can allow blocked paths for a ticket/chat or project; next run uses the new rules.

sources.title: Automations | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Recurring schedules and merged-PR events create tickets, launch runs or send messages; event duplication is suppressed and throttling is configurable.

sources.title: Workspaces | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Owner/Admin/Collaborator/Viewer permissions, membership and a recent-activity sidebar are documented; model credits differ from compute credits.

sources.title: Usage | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Dashboard separates actual metered API spend from token-equivalent value, with user/agent breakdowns and subscription coverage.

sources.title: Pricing | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: Free $0 uses a one-time 20000-credit grant; Pro starts at $50 monthly. Compute is per-second credit usage; seats are not separately billed.

sources.title: Security | Superconductor Docs
sources.finding: AWS hosting, encrypted sensitive data, RBAC, aggregate telemetry and 30-day account-closure deletion are stated. SOC 2 Type 2 is a goal, not an achieved assurance.

sources.title: Superconductor complete mobile client guide
sources.locator: iOS/iPad app download and Android app sections
sources.finding: The complete mobile guide distributes the native iOS/iPad app and instructs Android users to install the Chrome PWA. It lists no native Android package; PWA and native phone clients are separate options.

sources.title: Superconductor shipped delegation skills
sources.locator: Always-on skills; Creating tickets; Messaging other agents
sources.finding: The product injects skills into each non-benchmark agent. Agents can create and launch a ticket implementation, inspect its state, conversation and diff, and send instructions to another implementation/chat. Each message starts a new turn in the receiving agent. Scope is same-project work, except personal assistants can span the workspace.

sources.title: Superconductor application terms
sources.locator: Sections 2.2 Compute Infrastructure, 10 Intellectual Property and 19.3 License Grant; updated 2026-10-01
sources.finding: The service is owned by Volition and uses partner-provided compute infrastructure. Its mobile application has a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable use license. Open-source components retain separate component terms; the main service is not granted a standard open-source application license.
